notes: No invented Sn/Sp. Traditional MTrP maps labeled traditional. No Travell verbatim. SNOOP first.

relations.source_structure: possible secondary headache (vascular, infection, mass, trauma)
relations.clinical_context: Thunderclap, worst headache, focal neurology, fever/stiff neck, trauma with vomiting/confusion, or other SNOOP-type features.
supporting_evidence: Secondary-headache red-flag frameworks exist to trigger medical/emergency pathways
MSK or myofascial hypotheses are inappropriate first steps

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Safety screen, not a physiotherapy test accuracy claim.

limitations: SNOOP is a mnemonic, not a validated single score
Absence of red flags does not prove primary headache
recommended_examination: Urgent medical pathway per local protocol

references.citation: Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain: Revision 2017 (CPG). JOSPT — associated cervical red flags.
ICHD-3: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition — secondary vs primary framing (qualitative).

relations.source_structure: upper cervical somatic structures (clinical cervicogenic headache construct)
relations.clinical_context: Headache provoked or eased by neck movement/posture, with upper-cervical findings, after SNOOP screen.
supporting_evidence: Neck Pain CPGs include cervicogenic contribution as a clinical pattern
Evidence reviews emphasize overlap with primary headache and lack of a single confirmatory test

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: No isolated MSK test confirms cervicogenic headache. Do not invent Sn/Sp.

limitations: Migraine and cervicogenic features often coexist
Spurling does not diagnose headache source
recommended_examination: C0–C2 AROM and familiar-pain reproduction with cervical tests
Do not treat migraine features as trigger points

references.citation: Bogduk N, Govind J. Cervicogenic headache: an assessment of the evidence on diagnosis, management, and treatment. Lancet Neurol. 2009.
Blanpied PR et al. Neck Pain: Revision 2017 (CPG). JOSPT.

relations.clinical_context: Pulsatile headache with nausea/photophobia ± aura, or bilateral pressing tension-type pattern, with or without neck pain.
supporting_evidence: ICHD-3 classifies primary headache by pattern, not by a physical test
Neck pain does not exclude migraine

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: Pattern recognition, not Sn/Sp of palpation.

limitations: Neck pain is common in migraine
Do not relabel migraine as MTrP
recommended_examination: Cervical exam as adjunct, not replacement

references.citation: Headache Classification Committee of the IHS. The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition. Cephalalgia. 2018.

relations.clinical_context: Palpation reproduces familiar head pain after SNOOP and after primary vs cervicogenic framing.
supporting_evidence: Classical maps describe head referral from cervical/shoulder girdle muscles (traditional class only)

diagnostic_accuracy.notes: MTrP palpation reliability limited (Lucas 2009). Found ≠ cause.

limitations: Traditional maps are not absolute anatomy
Must not replace SNOOP or migraine reasoning
Do not attribute vertigo solely to SCM
recommended_examination: Familiar pain on palpation plus cervical AROM

references.citation: Tough EA et al. Variability of criteria used to diagnose myofascial trigger point pain syndrome. 2007.
Lucas N et al. Reliability of physical examination for diagnosis of myofascial trigger points. Clin J Pain. 2009.
